text: On behalf of the people of the 9th District of New York, the Clarke family, and myself, I wish to extend my heartfelt condolences to the many loved ones and countless fellow fans of the internationally renowned Mr. Slinger Francisco, the Mighty Sparrow, as we grieve this peerless icon’s transition to paradise. Though he was born in Grenada and raised in Trinidad and Tobago, the Mighty Sparrow’s talent was so substantial and his art so impactful, it could not be confined to the nations of the Caribbean, but instead came to be beloved across the globe. Indeed, the “Calypso King of the World” earned his crown through his remarkable talent, generous spirit, and unrelenting commitment to his craft. I have no doubt that incomparable legacy will persist long past the loss of our Legend. We will remember the Mighty Sparrow as a consummate entertainer, celebrate him as a cultural institution, and honor him as the trailblazer, charitable soul, and innovator he was. And, though our sorrow is great, may we find comfort in knowing that tonight, the Kingdom of Heaven will ring alive with sweet steel melodies and the songs and sounds of our people.

text:
Climate change is already making your life and your home more expensive.

Think they've got nothing to do with each other? Think again.

Canada has been hammered by wildfires, causing the price of Canadian lumber to skyrocket. Guess what we use a whole lot of to build homes here in the U.S.? Canadian lumber.

Then there's the heat. We are getting heat wave after heat wave, meaning your AC is working overtime, driving your electricity bill through the roof.

Then there are the natural disasters. More and more homes are being put at risk, and we're seeing it right here in California where homes in Dana Point are on the verge of collapsing.

Climate change is not some bill that comes due 50 years from now. We are already paying for it.

And the longer we wait to fix it, the bigger that bill gets.

I led a resolution to ensure that a predatory rule change to kick 2 million Americans off their health care and send costs soaring does not go into effect. Today, the Senate is voting on its companion to ensure everyone can access health care—not just the wealthy and well-connected.

I’m committed to making health care affordable and accessible, and I’ll work with anyone to get it done, regardless of their party or chamber. I urge my Senate colleagues to pass the resolution.

As election day approaches, it's crucial we raise awareness about what federal law says about protecting our vote. That's why Congresswoman Ramirez and I sat down with community groups, local government and election officials to hear what it takes to keep our elections running smoothly.

Let's be very clear: deploying ICE or any armed federal enforcement officers to polling places violates the law. So does voter intimidation, coercion, or any attempt to interfere with the right to vote.

So while Trump and his anti-democracy allies in Congress work to undermine confidence in our elections, Congresswoman Ramirez and I will fight just as hard to defend them.

quoted.text:
In the face of authoritarian attacks on our democracy, intergovernmental coalitions protect our elections and ensure every person’s vote is counted.

Yesterday, I joined @RepChuyGarcia to host an election protection roundtable with election officials, government agencies, community stakeholders, and other partners to discuss preparedness and coordination efforts to protect our elections.

Our message is clear: We will not be bullied, we will not be intimidated, and we will not let our constituents be dissuaded from exercising their constitutional rights.

I saw the damage from this Nor’easter firsthand in Brigantine today. Days of wind, waves, and flooding took a real toll on our coastline – washing away dunes, damaging beach ramps and fences, and leaving debris behind.

And the damage extends up and down our coast. Our Department of Environmental Protection surveyed beaches before and during the storm and is now deploying teams to document the damage, assess recovery needs, and work directly with impacted communities.

We were in close contact with local leaders before the storm hit, and we’ll continue working alongside them throughout the recovery. There’s a lot of work ahead, and it will take partnership at every level of government.

New Jersey takes care of its own, and we’ll be there for these communities every step of the way.

More than 100 of us asked Speaker Johnson to keep the House in session to vote on AI safeguards. 

He sent us home instead. 

Let's come back and get this done.

In a letter sent to Abbott’s office today, Hinojosa invokes a provision of the Texas Public Information Act governing information requested by lawmakers for legislative purposes. Hinojosa says the records could shed new light on Musk’s relationship with Abbott, including his companies’ lucrative state contracts and tax incentives, as well as Musk’s campaign contributions. She argues Musk has turned Texas into a corporate playground and says greater transparency is needed to expose what she describes as corruption in Abbott’s relationship with powerful tech interests.

She is requesting that Abbott’s office arrange an inspection of both the redacted and unredacted records on or around October 13.

Now Texans may finally learn what was considered so “intimate and embarrassing” that it was kept from public view.

🚨 BREAKING: Texas state Rep. Gina Hinojosa has filed an official request to inspect unredacted communications between Gov. Greg Abbott’s office and Elon Musk and his companies, after roughly 1,400 pages of records released last year were heavily redacted.

The state previously argued that portions of the communications could be withheld because they contained “intimate and embarrassing information.”

In a letter sent to Abbott’s office today, Hinojosa invokes a provision of the Texas Public Information Act governing information requested by lawmakers for legislative purposes. She is seeking the same records previously released to the Texas Newsroom, but “without any redactions whatsoever,” including material deemed “embarrassing” or “intimate.”

Hinojosa says the records could shed new light on Musk’s relationship with Abbott, including his companies’ lucrative state contracts and tax incentives, as well as Musk’s campaign contributions. She argues Musk has turned Texas into a corporate playground and says greater transparency is needed to expose what she describes as corruption in Abbott’s relationship with powerful tech interests.

She is requesting that Abbott’s office arrange an inspection of both the redacted and unredacted records on or around October 13.

Now Texans may finally learn what was considered so “intimate and embarrassing” that it was kept from public view.

Food insecurity remains a serious challenge for too many families. By connecting students with fresh food and practical food-literacy skills, this project is helping build a healthier, more food-secure Sacramento.

Thank you to Food Literacy Center, Leataata Floyd Elementary School, and the community partners bringing this vision to life.

text:
Last week, the Trump administration announced it is removing about 760,000 people from ACA coverage, saying they were fraudulently enrolled or “phantom” enrollees.

Nobody should be paying for coverage that doesn’t exist, and I support going after the brokers and bad actors who game the system. But an anti-fraud effort only works if it protects the people who did nothing wrong. 

Under this plan, enrollees who did not respond within 30 days of outreach had their coverage canceled, and critics warn that eligible families will get caught up in it.

The reality is that millions fewer people are enrolled in ACA coverage this year than last, because of Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill. 

Families should get clear notice and a real chance to appeal before anyone loses their coverage. 

We must stop the #GOPWarOnHealthcare and bring costs down.
